narrative.title: Repainting the Contiguous Rack Zones
narrative.scenario: A paint robot on a warehouse mezzanine receives one coordinate and a new shade. It repaints the crate under the nozzle, then rolls to the four edge-adjacent crates — but only across crates that currently wear the exact same shade as the starting one — continuing the spread until the whole matching zone wears the new colour. Crates of a different shade, even a step away, stay untouched.
narrative.inputFormat: An m x n integer grid image, a start cell (sr, sc), and an integer color.
narrative.outputFormat: Return the grid after repainting every cell 4-directionally connected to the start that shared the start's original colour.

testCases.explanation: The connected 1-zone around (1,1) turns 2; the far 1 is diagonally cut off and keeps its colour.
Repainting a zone with its own shade is a no-op everywhere.

hintLevels: Level 1: It is a connected-component recolour anchored at one cell.
Level 2: Capture the start's original shade first; spread only while a neighbour matches that exact shade.
Level 3: The 'not already the new colour' guard both prevents loops when color equals the source and short-circuits no-op fills.
